cases.sentence: Пожатие плеч и ___ не раздражили Левина.
cases.explain: «Улыбка» is one of the subjects of «не раздражили», so it stands in the Nominative case.
«Тарантаса» depends on the noun «грохот» ("rumble of something"), a Genitive of source.

cases.sentence: ___ жалко стало его и совестно за себя, хозяина дома.
cases.explain: «Левину» is the experiencer in the impersonal construction «жалко стало», hence Dative.

cases.sentence: Проходя через переднюю, он велел закладывать ___, чтобы ехать на станцию.
cases.explain: «Коляску» is the direct object of the transitive verb «закладывать», hence Accusative.

cases.sentence: «Я прошу вас объяснить мне с ___», — сказал он, поняв, наконец.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» governs the Instrumental case: «с достоинством».

cases.sentence: На ___ лежал обломок палки, которую они нынче утром вместе сломали на гимнастике.
cases.explain: The preposition «на» (location) governs the Prepositional case: «на столе».

reading.ru: Дарья Александровна с своей стороны была в этот день в большом огорчении.
reading.question: What was Darya Alexandrovna's mood that day?
options: She was excited about a visit
reading.explain: The text says Darya Alexandrovna, for her part, was in great distress that day.

reading.ru: Она с Гришей ходила в малину, и там...
reading.question: What was Masha accused of doing with Grisha?
options: Going into the raspberry patch and doing something Dolly could barely describe
Breaking a vase in the drawing room
reading.correct: Going into the raspberry patch and doing something Dolly could barely describe
reading.explain: Dolly explains that Masha went with Grisha into the raspberries, where something happened she could hardly bring herself to describe.

reading.ru: Мы поссорились второй раз с тех пор, как Стива приехал».
reading.question: What did Levin tell Dolly about his fight with Kitty?
options: It was the second time they had quarreled since Stiva arrived
It was their first quarrel ever
It happened because of the princess
reading.correct: It was the second time they had quarreled since Stiva arrived
reading.explain: Levin tells Dolly they had quarreled for the second time since Stiva arrived.

reading.ru: Не только я, но Стива заметил.
reading.question: Who else besides Dolly noticed Veslovsky's behavior toward Kitty?
reading.explain: Dolly says it was not only she who noticed, but Stiva noticed too, that Veslovsky was flirting a little with Kitty.

reading.ru: «Ну и прекрасно. Теперь я спокоен. Я прогоню его», — сказал Левин.
reading.question: What did Levin decide to do once Dolly confirmed his suspicions?
options: He decided to send Veslovsky away
He decided to apologize to Kitty
He decided to leave the house himself
He decided to say nothing further
reading.correct: He decided to send Veslovsky away
reading.explain: Levin says he is now calm and will drive Veslovsky away.

reading.ru: Девочка разрыдалась, зарылась лицом в коленях матери, и Долли положила ей на голову свою худую нежную руку.
reading.question: How did the scene with Masha end?
options: Masha burst into tears and buried her face in her mother's lap while Dolly comforted her
Masha ran off to play outside
Masha was sent to bed without supper
Masha apologized calmly and left the room
reading.correct: Masha burst into tears and buried her face in her mother's lap while Dolly comforted her
reading.explain: The text describes Masha bursting into sobs and burying her face in her mother's knees, while Dolly laid her thin, gentle hand on her head.

reading.ru: Проходя через переднюю, он велел закладывать коляску, чтобы ехать на станцию.
reading.question: What did Levin order as he went to find Veslovsky?
options: He ordered the carriage to be harnessed to go to the station
He ordered his horse saddled for hunting
He ordered tea to be served
He ordered the servants to pack Veslovsky's bags
reading.correct: He ordered the carriage to be harnessed to go to the station
reading.explain: Passing through the hall, he ordered the carriage harnessed to go to the station.

reading.ru: Левин застал Васеньку в то время, как тот, разобрав свои вещи из чемодана и разложив новые романсы, примеривал краги, чтоб ездить верхом.
reading.question: What was Vasenka doing when Levin found him?
options: Trying on riding gaiters after unpacking his suitcase and laying out new romances
Writing a letter to a friend
reading.correct: Trying on riding gaiters after unpacking his suitcase and laying out new romances
reading.explain: Levin found Vasenka trying on gaiters for riding, having unpacked his suitcase and laid out new romances.

reading.ru: Он был, несомненно, добрый малый, и Левину жалко стало его и совестно за себя, хозяина дома, когда он подметил робость во взгляде Васеньки.
reading.question: How did Levin feel when he noticed timidity in Vasenka's eyes?
options: Sorry for him and ashamed of himself as host
reading.correct: Sorry for him and ashamed of himself as host
reading.explain: The text says Levin felt sorry for Vasenka, undoubtedly a good fellow, and ashamed of himself as host when he noticed the timidity in Vasenka's look.

reading.question: What did Levin finally say to Vasenka after struggling to begin?
options: That he had ordered the horses to be harnessed for him
That the princess wanted to see him
reading.correct: That he had ordered the horses to be harnessed for him
reading.explain: Levin tells Vasenka that he has ordered the horses harnessed for him, signaling he must leave.

reading.ru: «Вам на железную дорогу», — мрачно сказал Левин, щипля конец палки.
reading.question: Where did Levin tell Vasenka he must go?
options: Back to Moscow with the princess
reading.explain: Levin gloomily tells him he must go to the railway station.

reading.question: What did Vasenka ask for after realizing he was being asked to leave?
options: To see Kitty one more time
reading.explain: After bowing with a shrug, Vasenka asks whether he might see Oblonsky.

reading.ru: «Что это за бессмыслица?» — говорил Степан Аркадьевич, узнав от приятеля, что его выгоняют из дому и найдя Левина в саду, где он гулял, дожидаясь отъезда гостя.
reading.question: How did Stepan Arkadyich react on learning Veslovsky was being sent away?
options: He called it nonsense and confronted Levin in the garden
He laughed it off and ignored it
He immediately packed to leave with Veslovsky
reading.correct: He called it nonsense and confronted Levin in the garden
reading.explain: Stepan Arkadyich exclaimed "What nonsense is this?" upon learning his friend was being expelled, and found Levin in the garden.

reading.ru: Мне очень совестно пред тобой и пред ним.
reading.question: What did Levin admit to Stepan Arkadyich about the situation?
options: That he felt very ashamed before him and before Veslovsky
That Kitty had asked him to do it
That he wanted Stepan Arkadyich to apologize instead
reading.correct: That he felt very ashamed before him and before Veslovsky
reading.explain: Levin says he feels very ashamed before Stepan Arkadyich and before Veslovsky, though he could not act otherwise.

reading.ru: Скоро он услыхал грохот тарантаса и увидал из-за деревьев, как Васенька, сидя на сене, на беду не было сиденья в тарантасе, в своей шотландской шапочке, подпрыгивая по толчкам, проехал по аллее.
reading.question: How did Levin see Vasenka leave the estate?
options: Sitting on hay in the tarantass, since there was no seat, jolting along in his Scottish cap
Being driven off in a comfortable carriage
reading.correct: Sitting on hay in the tarantass, since there was no seat, jolting along in his Scottish cap
reading.explain: Levin saw Vasenka, sitting on hay because there was no seat in the tarantass, bouncing along in his Scottish cap as he was driven down the avenue.

reading.ru: Степан Аркадьевич и княгиня были возмущены поступком Левина.
reading.question: How did Stepan Arkadyich and the princess feel about what Levin had done?
options: They were indignant at his action
reading.correct: They were indignant at his action
reading.explain: The text states that Stepan Arkadyich and the princess were indignant at Levin's action.

reading.ru: И Долли, имевшая от отца дар смешно рассказывать, заставляла падать от смеха Вареньку, когда она в третий и четвертый раз, все с новыми юмористическими прибавлениями, рассказывала, как она только что собралась надеть новые бантики для гостя и выходила уж в гостиную, вдруг услыхала грохот Колымаги.
reading.question: How did the household's mood change by evening, and what did Dolly do?
options: Everyone grew unusually lively and cheerful, and Dolly retold the story of Vasenka's departure, making Varenka laugh
Everyone remained gloomy and silent all evening
The princess forgave Levin and celebrated
Dolly refused to speak about the incident at all
reading.correct: Everyone grew unusually lively and cheerful, and Dolly retold the story of Vasenka's departure, making Varenka laugh
reading.explain: By evening everyone but the princess had become unusually animated and merry, and Dolly, who had her father's gift for comic storytelling, made Varenka laugh retelling the story of Vasenka's expulsion.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Darya's distress about the children's misbehavior?
sentences: Проводив жену наверх, Левин пошел на половину Долли.
Дарья Александровна с своей стороны была в этот день в большом огорчении.
Она ходила по комнате и сердито говорила стоявшей в углу и ревущей девочке:
highlight.explain: This sentence describes her angry words to the crying girl about what happened with the berries.

highlight.question: Which sentence indicates the children went somewhere and did something inappropriate?
sentences: – Они с Гришей ходили в малину и там…  я не могу даже сказать, что она делала.
Вот какие гадости.
Тысячу раз пожалеешь miss Elliot.
Эта ни за чем не смотрит, машина…
Figurez vous, qu'elle…
highlight.explain: This sentence shows that the children went to pick berries and Darya witnessed behavior she cannot even speak of.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Levin asking his guest to depart?
sentences: – Что ты, Костя, опомнись!
– смеясь, сказала она.
– Ну, можешь идти теперь к Фанни, – сказала она Маше.
– Нет, уж если хочешь ты, то я скажу Стиве.
Он увезет его.
highlight.explain: This sentence contains Levin's request that the guest leave, where he cannot hide from his obligation.

highlight.question: Which sentence expresses shock that being expelled from the house is considered ridiculous?
sentences: – Случилось, что я жду гостей, – сказал Левин, быстрее и быстрее обламывая сильными пальцами концы расщепившейся палки.
– И не жду гостей, и ничего не случилось, но я прошу вас уехать.
Вы можете объяснить как хотите мою неучтивость.
highlight.explain: This sentence is Stepan's exclamation of absurdity when he learns that his host is actually asking him to leave.

highlight.question: Which sentence reveals that Levin had forgotten about the machine driver?
sentences: – Что это за бессмыслица!
– говорил Степан Аркадьич, узнав от приятеля, что его выгоняют из дому, и найдя Левина в саду, где он гулял, дожидаясь отъезда гостя.
– Mais c'est ridicule!
Какая тебя муха укусила?
Mais c'est du dernier ridicule!
Что же тебе показалось, если молодой человек…
highlight.explain: This sentence indicates the machine driver was someone Levin had completely forgotten about.
